LESSON: MELODY IN MAJOR KEYS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Foundations of Music and Dance
Topic 1.2: Melody in Major Keys
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 11

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Melody in Major Keys, part of Foundations of Music and Dance in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: What is a melody? 2. How is melodic interest created in music?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to or sing songs in simple time and familiar tunes in major keys and identify melodic devices used. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech, hum, mime or use 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to or sing songs in simple time and familiar tunes in major keys and identify melodic devices used. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech, hum, mime or use 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Melody in Major Keys together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: The learner listens critically and speaks/mimes clearly while critiquing melodies

written by self and others.

• Self-efficacy: The learner gains confidence as they sing /hum/mime or play composed melodies.

• Creativity and imagination: The learner comes up with new musical ideas when composing melodies.

• Digital literacy: The learner uses appropriate assistive digital devices to store composed music in a digital portfolio.

Values:
8

• Respect: The learner appreciates others’ views when giving and receiving feedback on their compositions.

• Integrity: The learner creates original music without plagiarism.

• Social justice: The learner shares learning resources and ideas with peers when creating music.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Peace education: The learner uses techniques learnt in music composition to compose songs on peace.

• Cyber security: The learner uses digital apps responsibly.

Suggested Learning Resources

Sheet music, Flash cards of melodic motifs, Audio/visual recordings of songs, Portfolios, Anecdotal records, Manuscript

books, Text books, Pitching device, Song book, ICT devices and Internet connectivity
